Find the area $A$ of the region in the $xy$-plane that is bounded by the curve $y=-5{cos}^{2}\,(\frac{x}{2})+5{sin}^{2}\,(\frac{x}{2})+4x+7,$ the $x$-axis and the lines $x=-\frac{\pi }{2}$ and $x=0,$ as shown above. Do not round the answer.

$A=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
The area of the region is given by

$$
A={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{0}(-5{cos}^{2}\,(\frac{x}{2})+5{sin}^{2}\,(\frac{x}{2})+4x+7)\,\text{d}x.
$$

To calculate this integral, we use the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2x={cos}^{2}⁡x-{sin}^{2}⁡x
$$

We can rewrite the above formula as

$$
-5\operatorname{cos}⁡x=-5{cos}^{2}\,(\frac{x}{2})+5{sin}^{2}\,(\frac{x}{2}).
$$

Hence, the area of the region is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{0}(-5{cos}^{2}\,(\frac{x}{2})+5{sin}^{2}\,(\frac{x}{2})+4x+7)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{0}(-5\operatorname{cos}⁡x+4x+7)\,\text{d}x \\  & =(-5\operatorname{sin}⁡x+2{x}^{2}+7x)\,{|}_{-\pi /2}^{0} \\  & =[-5\operatorname{sin}⁡0+2(0)^{2}+7\cdot 0]-[-5\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\frac{\pi }{2})+2{(-\frac{\pi }{2})}^{2}+7(-\frac{\pi }{2})] \\  & =0-[5+\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{2}-\frac{7\pi }{2}] \\  & =-5-\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{2}+\frac{7\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 7

Find the area A of the region in the xy-plane that is bounded by the curve y=−5cos2(x2)+5sin2(x2)+4x+7, the x-axis and the lines x=−π2 and x=0, as shown above. Do not round the answer.
A=
7π2​−π22​−5

Correct
EXPLANATION

The area of the region is given by A=∫−π/20(−5cos2(x2)+5sin2(x2)+4x+7)dx.

To calculate this integral, we use the double-angle formula for cosine: cos⁡2x=cos2⁡x−sin2⁡x

We can rewrite the above formula as −5cos⁡x=−5cos2(x2)+5sin2(x2).

Hence, the area of the region is

A=∫−π/20(−5cos2(x2)+5sin2(x2)+4x+7)dx=∫−π/20(−5cos⁡x+4x+7)dx=(−5sin⁡x+2x2+7x)|−π/20=[−5sin⁡0+2(0)2+7⋅0]−[−5sin⁡(−π2)+2(−π2)2+7(−π2)]=0−[5+π22−7π2]=−5−π22+7π2.
